headline: Ukraine Strikes Key Russian Rocket Factory, Imperiling Space Program
deck: Ukraine's use of long-range cruise missiles to hit a critical space center in Samara threatens Russia's satellite and human spaceflight capabilities.
body: Ukraine struck Russia's Progress Rocket Space Center in Samara, using ground-launched cruise missiles to target a facility critical for military satellites and human spaceflight.
The Progress Rocket Space Center serves as a vital hub for Russia's aerospace industry. It handles electronics production, assembles the Soyuz-2 and Soyuz-5 rockets, and builds military satellites.

The attack utilized FP-5 'Flamingo' missiles, weapons known for their range of several thousand kilometers. This strike demonstrates Ukraine's expanding capability to reach deep into Russian territory.

The Soyuz-2 family of rockets forms the backbone of Russia's space launches, accounting for over 85 percent of all Russian rocket deployments since 2020. These workhorse vehicles can lift about 8 metric tons to low-Earth orbit.
Notably, the Soyuz-2 rocket also carries Russia's human spacecraft for missions to the International Space Station. Damage to its production facility could disrupt critical crew transport operations.
The strike exacerbates existing strains on Russia's space ambitions. Demand for Soyuz rockets already exceeds production capacity by 30 to 50 percent for the period between 2027 and 2030.
Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed the attack, stating, "Flamingo missiles were used. A good achievement."

The attack, hitting a facility approximately 900 km from the Ukrainian border, signals a new phase in the conflict's reach. Russia now faces significant challenges to its strategic space infrastructure and future launch capabilities.
